summary: Ulster County, NY 60-ft Aermotor LS40 lookout built on Gallis Hill in 1927; moved in 1950 to Overlook Mountain, where it stands restored.

facts.status_note: Taken down from Gallis Hill in 1950 and moved to Overlook Mountain, where it still stands restored. No source describes what, if anything, remains on Gallis Hill.

events.note: Built by the Conservation Department as a 60-ft Aermotor LS40 steel tower, with an observer cabin of the 1922 standard design erected at the same time.
Hunters shot out observatory windows when the tower opened for the season; the state promised a $500 fine for the culprits (quoting The Kingston Daily Freeman).

Observer M. Edison reported a fire in the Stony Hollow section; Deputy Sheriff Ray Winne gathered a crew of ten men, and the fire broke out again that night, when fire fighters stayed on duty all night.
Observer G.F. Edson had served eleven years at the tower, per the Kingston paper of September 14, 1940.
Tower closed, disassembled and taken off Gallis Hill.
Moved about eight miles north to a new site on Overlook Mountain, where it still stands.
Catskill fire towers, including Overlook, were closed for safety reasons in 1988 (Wikipedia); Overlook reopened June 5, 1999.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia places the hill northwest of Kingston; the NYSFFLA chapter gives three miles northeast. The story says only 'a few miles from Kingston' and reports the disagreement.

resolved_conflicts.field: origin of the Overlook Mountain tower
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR Overlook page dates that tower to 1917. Wikipedia and the NYSFFLA chapter say it was first erected on Gallis Hill in 1927 and moved in 1950. The story follows the 1927 account and reports the register's date.

resolved_conflicts.field: closing year of the Overlook tower
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR page says it closed in 1971; Wikipedia says the Catskill towers were closed for safety reasons in 1988. The story gives no single closing year for the Overlook tower.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 'gone' is right for the Gallis Hill site, but the tower itself stands on Overlook Mountain (NHLR US 223, NY 17). That structure deserves its own or a linked record. Sources disagree on the Gallis Hill direction from Kingston (northwest per Wikipedia, northeast per NYSFFLA) and on the Overlook tower's origin (1917 per NHLR, 1927 on Gallis Hill per Wikipedia and NYSFFLA) and closing year (1971 per NHLR, 1988 per Wikipedia). The Overlook conflicts belong on the Overlook record. The 1928 newspaper spells the hill 'gallows Hill'. No source describes the Gallis Hill site today, so no access level is recorded for it. Two FFLA Facebook posts that mention the tower were found in search but could not be read, so they are not cited and no photos were added.
